key_insight: Period-shifted DMD identifies Floquet multipliers and time-periodic modes, capturing stability in periodic systems that a single constant snapshot-to-snapshot operator cannot represent.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports stability analysis of periodically varying flows and structures, including combustors observed through velocity, scalar, or acoustic measurements.
method: FD applies DMD to snapshots subsampled once per period.
EFD stacks all snapshots within each period to recover shared multipliers and phase-resolved modes.
Both are exact for linear time-periodic systems when measurements determine the state: at one phase for FD, or across a period for EFD.
evidence_signal: The methods are verified against known multipliers and illustrated with velocity, scalar, and acoustic-pressure measurements from a swirl-stabilized combustor.
watch_item: For nonlinear or noisy data, estimated multiplier moduli can be biased and should not be interpreted as decay rates; period, rank, and data scaling require care.
paper_title: Floquet Decomposition: Floquet Multipliers and Time-Periodic Modes from Period-Sampled Snapshot Data
